g0.rationale: RESOLVED BY R1 (2026-09-14): the charter's named example was mistaken on the facts and has been corrected; this product is eligible, mode-scoped. The §2.2 five-step derivation below is unchanged and is now the charter's own worked case. || THE COHORT'S OPEN G0 QUESTION, RESOLVED AGAINST THE CHARTER'S ASSUMPTION. §2.2's five-step test run verbatim on the frozen directions. STEP 1 — authoritative directions located: 'Als Spülung (für sofortige Regeneration): ins gewaschene, nasse Haar einmassieren, kurz einwirken lassen (ca. 30 Sekunden) und gut ausspülen. Als Kur (für Tiefenregeneration): ins gewaschene, nasse Haar einmassieren, 2-3 Minuten einwirken lassen und genießen, dann ausspülen.' STEP 2 — test each stated mode against §2.1. Mode A 'Als Spülung': after cleansing YES ('ins gewaschene, nasse Haar'); stated contact time YES (ca. 30 Sekunden); rinse YES ('gut ausspülen'); but the mode is self-labelled a Spülung, i.e. a conditioner, and §2.1's category definition requires a rinse-out INTENSIVE TREATMENT (Haarkur/Maske). Mode A is a conditioner mode. Mode B 'Als Kur': after cleansing YES (identical wording); stated contact time YES (2–3 Minuten); rinse YES ('dann ausspülen'); self-labelled a Kur and explicitly purposed 'für Tiefenregeneration'. Mode B IS a qualifying rinse-out mask mode. STEP 3 — exactly one mode qualifies as a MASK mode → classify only that mode, record multi_use: true, name the uncovered mode. STEP 4 not reached (a mode does qualify). STEP 5 not reached: the directions are NOT ambiguous about which mode carries which dwell — the modes are separately named, separately purposed, and carry distinct stated contact times — so `multi_use_directions_ambiguity` does NOT fire. Charter F1 is what governs, and F1's own text says a multi-use product is eligible 'when authoritative directions state a distinct rinse-out mask mode with dwell'. These directions do exactly that.
evidenceSignals: directions mode B verbatim: 'Als Kur (für Tiefenregeneration): ins gewaschene, nasse Haar einmassieren, 2-3 Minuten einwirken lassen und genießen, dann ausspülen'
directions mode A verbatim: 'Als Spülung (für sofortige Regeneration): … kurz einwirken lassen (ca. 30 Sekunden) und gut ausspülen'

the two modes are separately named ('Als Spülung' / 'Als Kur'), separately purposed ('sofortige Regeneration' / 'Tiefenregeneration'), and carry distinct contact times — they are separable, so §2.2 step 5 is not reached
charter F2 (binding): dwell is protocol metadata under P5 and is NEVER a boundary test, so the shortness of either mode cannot decide eligibility
charter F1: eligible when authoritative directions state a distinct rinse-out mask mode with dwell

charterResolution.ruling: R1 (Nick, 2026-09-14) — CORRECT THE CHARTER. The directions test decides (charter F1); the 2–3-minute Kur mode is mask territory; classification is mode-scoped.
charterResolution.what_was_wrong: The charter's exclusion rested on the factual premise that this product's only rinse-out mode is a short conditioner mode. The frozen directions falsify that premise: there are two rinse-out modes, and the second is a self-labelled Kur with a 2–3 minute stated dwell and a Tiefenregeneration purpose. v0.1's AP-12-CHARTERFLIP escalated exactly this, offering resolution (A) correct the example or (B) write a label-based 2in1 exclusion narrowing F1. Nick ruled (A). Standard v0.2 §2.1 and §2.2 are rewritten accordingly, and §2.2 now carries this product as the worked case rather than as the excluded example.
charterResolution.restated_principle: No MODE is ever profiled twice. A multi-mode product may hold ONE profile per engine, each covering exactly one mode. This product's Conditioner-engine profile for the 30-second Spülung mode is untouched and not in conflict with the mask profile for its Kur mode.
charterResolution.status: RESOLVED. The profile in this record is OFFICIAL, not provisional. The v0.1 withdrawal scenario ('if Nick rules (B), this record's entire profile is withdrawn') is void.

tailMarker.anomalyNote: No §3.1 anomaly. Read as a closed enumeration, it is not a marker and tail_index stays at 12. Had it counted, the credited segment would shrink from eleven entries to six, S3 would fail, and conditioning_level would drop from high to moderate. See AP-12-CHELATOR.  ||  TAIL MARKER RE-CHECKED UNDER v0.2 (R8 tail-class union list + R2 plausibility). v0.1's AP-12-CHELATOR turned on whether TETRASODIUM GLUTAMATE DIACETATE @7 is tail-class; the standard's §3.1 list and lexicon §0.2/§10 now carry ONE reconciled union list and TETRASODIUM GLUTAMATE DIACETATE is explicitly ON it (R8, 2026-09-14). ETHYLHEXYLGLYCERIN @9 is likewise now marker-eligible, as a preservative booster declared alongside PHENOXYETHANOL @12. The earliest marker-eligible species is therefore TETRASODIUM GLUTAMATE DIACETATE @7, not PHENOXYETHANOL @12: tail_index moves from 12 to 7 and the credited segment shrinks from eleven entries to six. AP-12-CHELATOR is closed by rule, in the direction v0.1 flagged as the more honest one. PLAUSIBILITY ASSESSMENT (R2, §3.1.1): PLAUSIBLE - CETEARYL ALCOHOL @2, BEHENTRIMONIUM CHLORIDE @3 and CETYL ESTERS @5 outrank @7, and the product is a conventional O/W emulsion with AQUA @1. AVENA SATIVA KERNEL OIL @11, which carried S3 in v0.1, is now an ordinary tail member and carries nothing.  ||  RE-CHECKED UNDER v0.3 (E1, E2). E2's third plausibility limb does NOT fire: TETRASODIUM GLUTAMATE DIACETATE @7 is a chelator, its class is not ordered against any other tail class on this list in a contradictory way, and the list's fragrance entries (PARFUM @13, VANILLIN @14) sit BELOW the preservative block (ETHYLHEXYLGLYCERIN @9, PHENOXYETHANOL @12) in an ordinarily consistent arrangement; no declared allergen outranks its own PARFUM. It carries no S1/S2/S3 signal and no §9.2 term, and it was already counted in full toward the §9.5.3 humectant cluster, so it is NOT load-bearing for any value and no `boundary_position_ingredient` flag fires.

adjudicationPoints.title: E4 moves weight to `low` as ruled — and, via §9.5.2 step 3, ALSO moves primary_focus from `general` to `lightness`. ESCALATION: the ruling names the weight effect only
adjudicationPoints.body: E4's stated expectation is '#12 Guhl 2in1 → light', and the weight move is exactly that: all three conjuncts of the restated leanness test are positively observed (no R4b heavy lipid at any rank, no silicone at any rank, one cationic species at any rank), on a resolved and plausible marker. What the ruling does not mention is that `weight_potential: low` is one of only two conditions §9.5.2 step 3 requires for the `lightness` focus, and the other — `body_lightness_potential: likely_preserving` — has been on this record since v0.1. Step 3 is tested BEFORE moisture, shine and smoothing, so a candidate clearing there stops the hierarchy before step 8's `general` fallback. Applying the standard as written therefore gives `lightness`, and the v0.2 record predicted precisely this ('only the weight anchor's cetearyl conjunct blocks it'). The value is recorded as the standard produces it and the divergence from the ruling's scope is flagged rather than forced in either direction — the same treatment AP-01-TAILEDGEDROP and AP-11-COCONUT received. WHAT NICK DECIDES: whether `lightness` is the right HEADLINE for a lean conventional Kur, or whether step 3's two-condition test is too thin to sit above moisture/shine/smoothing in the hierarchy. Three things are worth weighing. (1) The route is reached on formula evidence alone — this pack carries no lightness, volume or 'ohne zu beschweren' positioning at all, so nothing here is claim-driven. (2) Watch-list item 2 recorded an expectation that `lightness` would go unused in this category; that expectation was formed while `low` was unreachable, so E4 falsifies its premise rather than its conclusion. (3) The focus value is a strict function of the weight value: hold weight at `moderate` and the focus returns to `general`. Approving one approves the other. Carried into the standard as §18 open question 13.
